 KRA tax returns deadline 2027: What you need to know about the new April 30 date
 Sunday 01st November, 2026 02:36 PM | 
 By Faith Lagat 
 Times Tower, the head offices of Kenya Revenue Authority. PHOTO/@3AKRACorporate/X 
 The Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA) has changed the deadline for individual taxpayers to file annual income tax returns, moving it from June 30 to April 30 from 2027.
 In a post on October 29, 2026, the official KRA Care account stated: “From 1st January 2027, individual taxpayers will be required to file their Income Tax Returns by 30th April, following changes introduced by the Finance Act 2026.”
 The new deadline will first apply to returns for the 2026 year of income, which taxpayers will file in 2027.
 The change means individual taxpayers will have to complete their annual returns by the last day of the fourth month after the end of the year of income.
 For taxpayers whose income year runs from January to December, the deadline will therefore be April 30.
 What the new KRA deadline means
 The revised filing calendar was introduced through the Finance Act 2026, changing the timeline that taxpayers have used for annual income tax returns.
 Previously, individual taxpayers generally had until June 30 of the following year to file their returns. The new timeline brings the deadline forward by two months.
 The change is aimed at spreading tax filing activity across the year and reducing pressure on KRA’s iTax system during the final days of the filing period.
 Individual taxpayers, including salaried employees and self-employed persons, will need to prepare their returns earlier under the new timeline.
 Salaried employees whose income is fully taxed through Pay As You Earn (PAYE ) will also fall under the April 30 deadline.
 Taxpayers filing returns for the 2025 year of income are not affected by the new deadline. Where applicable, those returns continue to follow the June 30, 2026 filing deadline.
 What about nil returns and companies?
 Taxpayers who have no taxable income will have an earlier deadline under the revised framework.
 Nil returns will be due by January 31 of the following year. This applies to taxpayers such as unemployed individuals, students, inactive PIN holders and others with no taxable income who are required to file returns.
 KRA post. PHOTO/A screengrab by PD Digital/@KRACare/X 
 Companies and other non-individual taxpayers will continue to operate under a different filing timeline.
 They are required to file by the last day of the sixth month after the end of their accounting period. For a company whose accounting year ends in December, the deadline remains June 30.
 The revised individual filing deadline therefore does not mean that all taxpayers will have the same April 30 deadline.
 Penalties and what taxpayers should prepare
 Taxpayers who fail to file their returns on time may face penalties. For individuals, the late filing penalty is 5 per cent of the tax due or Ksh2,000, whichever is higher.
 Any balance of tax due is generally payable by the April 30 filing deadline.
 KRA has advised taxpayers to prepare their records early as the new deadline approaches. Employees should have documents such as P9 forms, withholding certificates and records relating to tax reliefs available when filing their returns.
 The authority has also continued to expand digital filing options, including pre-filled returns for employment income.
 Taxpayers should ensure their PIN details and contact information are up to date on iTax and follow further guidance issued by KRA as the new filing calendar takes effect.
 The first major deadline under the new system will be January 31, 2027, for applicable nil returns, followed by April 30, 2027, for individual income tax returns.
